text:
Tom Willander's second season in Vancouver is becoming the story of the Canucks' November. He came back from a two-week absence on Nov. 13, and since then new coach Manny Malhotra has leaned on him, including 23.9 minutes against Vegas. The New York Times wrote about his "expanded role," and Daniel Wagner of Pass it to Bulis posted that "There's a case to be made that Tom Willander has been the #Canucks second-most impactful skater this season."

The Canucks get only about 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, but they are far worse without him: he sits almost seven points above his teammates. He has no goals and four assists in 21 games.

It's a big turn from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating noticeably more with him on the ice (bottom 3% of defensemen), though they noted his teammates were among the weakest in the league. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his knack for getting to the home-plate area in front of the net (83rd percentile for chances there). The 11th pick in 2023 is still only 21.
